steps.say: Giant cell arteritis is the disease past 50 with granulomas in large arteries. Jaw pain on chewing is the most specific symptom. Vision loss is the feared complication. Steroids start on suspicion, never after biopsy.
steps.tx: Past **50 years**, headache with chewing fatigue is **GCA** (giant cell arteritis, granulomatous disease of large arteries) until proven otherwise, busiest at **70 to 80 years** in women at 3 to 1. Tired jaws carry likelihood ratio above **4.0** for a positive biopsy, the sharpest cranial clue: **jaw claudication** (maxillary ischemia on chewing). Same-day steroids with urgent workup follow any such story.

vis.alt: Transmural granulomatous inflammation with luminal stenosis in temporal arteritis.
vis.caption: Granulomas with giant cells narrow the temporal artery lumen. Jaw claudication indicates this histology. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Classification needs age 50 or older plus 6 points across clinical, lab, and imaging domains. ESR above 50 and CRP above 10 count as lab points. Morning stiffness, jaw pain, vision loss, scalp pain, and vessel signs count clinically.
steps.tx: Under 2022 ACR EULAR rules, nobody below **50 years** enters classification; beyond that birthday, **6 points** or more across clinics (stiffness, jaw, vision, scalp, vessel signs), labs (**ESR 50 mm** per hour or higher with **CRP 10 mg** per L or higher), and scans or histology confirms GCA. Points without the entry age never classify, whatever the total.

steps.say: Blindness hits 15 to 20 percent of untreated patients through anterior optic nerve ischaemia. Sudden painless altitudinal loss with a pale swollen disc is the definition. The second eye follows within days without treatment. Vision symptoms are never watched.
steps.tx: Permanent visual loss hits **15 to 20 percent** of untreated patients, usually anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (**AION**, optic nerve head infarction) from short posterior ciliary occlusion, with sudden painless altitudinal deficit and pale swollen disc. The second eye follows within days without therapy. Any visual symptom in suspected GCA indicates IV methylprednisolone at once.

steps.say: Biopsy needs 1 to 2 cm length for skip lesions with granulomas and shattered elastic lamina. The halo sign gives 75 percent sensitivity with above 95 percent specificity. Treatment never waits for either test. A negative biopsy with high suspicion is still treated.
steps.tx: A **1 cm to 2 cm** arterial harvest defeats **skip lesions** (patchy wall inflammation), exposing transmural granulomas, shattered elastic lamina, giant cells, and heaped intima. The Doppler **halo sign** (dark incompressible wall ring) detects three quarters (**75 percent** sensitivity) with above **95 percent** specificity among experts. Neither result is awaited, because steroids start on suspicion.

steps.say: Prednisone 40 to 60 mg daily starts at once with pulse methylprednisolone for visual symptoms. Doses run 500 to 1000 mg daily for 3 days. Biopsy follows within days under steroid cover. Delay is the risk of the second eye.
steps.tx: Tablets first, drips for eyes: oral **prednisone 40 mg to 60 mg** daily opens at once, while visual symptoms or amaurosis fugax upgrade to IV **methylprednisolone 500 mg to 1,000 mg** daily across **3 days**. The biopsy is harvested days later under steroid cover, with histology intact. Proof never precedes pills, because the second eye does not wait.

steps.say: Tocilizumab 162 mg weekly or fortnightly with a 26-week taper gives 56 percent remission against 14 percent. Steroid load falls dramatically. It suits relapsing and large vessel disease. Tuberculosis and bowel screens come before it.
steps.tx: Steroid-free calm at one year separates GiACTA arms: **tocilizumab 162 mg** under the skin weekly or fortnightly, riding a **26-week** prednisone taper, held **56 percent** in remission versus **14 percent** at **52 weeks** on steroids alone. Relapsing and large vessel patterns suit IL-6 blockade best. Tuberculosis latency with bowel weak spots is excluded first, as before any biologic.

steps.say: Polymyalgia rheumatica gives shoulder and pelvic girdle pain with morning stiffness in the same age group. ESR and CRP run high together. Low dose steroids bring dramatic relief. Overlap with GCA is sought in every case.
steps.tx: Polymyalgia rheumatica (**PMR**, girdle pain and stiffness disease) brings bilateral shoulder and pelvic girdle synovitis with morning stiffness past 50, with high ESR and CRP. Low dose glucocorticoids bring dramatic relief within days. Up to a fifth overlap with GCA, so headache, jaw, vision, and large vessel symptoms are sought in every PMR case.

vis.alt: Bilateral shoulder and pelvic girdle synovitis with subacromial bursitis in polymyalgia rheumatica.
vis.caption: Girdle synovitis with bursitis marks PMR in the same age group as GCA. Overlap symptoms are sought always. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Large vessel patterns need whole aorta imaging with arch stenosis and aneurysm surveys. PET-CT with MR angiography are the mappers of the extent. Aneurysms are followed for years. Cranial and large vessel disease are treated with the same urgency.
steps.tx: Large vessel GCA needs whole aorta imaging: arch stenosis with elastic lamina fragmentation and medium-artery beaded **microaneurysms** (tiny ballooned segments) below, with aneurysm surveillance for years. **PET-CT** with MR angiography maps extent beyond cranial branches. Clot-free aortic wall thickening with high uptake indicates active large vessel disease on top of cranial symptoms.

vis.alt: Aortic arch stenosis with elastic lamina fragmentation and beaded medium-artery microaneurysms.
vis.caption: Arch disease with beaded aneurysms extends GCA beyond cranial branches. Whole tree imaging maps it. Credit: StewardMD.
